text.p: The Bear Stearns brokerage said in a report Monday it had downgraded financial group GF Bancomer from neutral to unattractive in the wake of 1996 results posted jan 31.

"We are reducing our estimates for 1997 from $0.79 to $0.45 per ADR and downgrading the stock from Neutral to Unattractive, basically due to higher than expected asset quality problems and a shrinking net interest margin," said analyst Alberto Sanchez in a report.
"The group also received substantial aid from the government via what some of its competitors refer to as midnight-Fobaproa loan sales," Sanchez added.
Fobaproa is the Mexico's Bank Insurance Fund, an organism to which Bancomer sold 12.3 billion pesos of past-due loans in January in exchange for 8 billion pesos in government securities.
Sanchez noted the huge loss arising from the difference between these two amounts (4.3 billion pesos) was charged directly against equity rather than appearing on the income statement.

"We though that since April 1995 this kind of practice was no longer permitted, but obviously the Mexican authorities had to agree in order to avoid banks from showing enormous losses," Sanchez added.
